html: The Wurla, also written Ola and shown on the map as Worla from 1600 to 1815, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland Kimberley of Western Australia. Little is recorded about them. Their country lay in the ranges between the Ngarinyin to the north, the Kija to the east and the Bunuba and Unggumi to the south. Cattle stations reached this rugged country only in the early 1900s.
